JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19.03.2020.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 19.03.2020 at about 01.00 a.m, the petitioner was travelling as a cleaner cum loader sleeping in the cabin of the lorry bearing no. KA-01-AK-0904 and the said lorry was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, while so proceeding on Bengaluru- Mangaluru NH-75 road, near Vaderahalli gate,
Vaderahalli village, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk,
the driver of the said lorry lost control over the vehicle and dashed against another lorry, which was going ahead of this lorry.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G. Nagar, wherein first aid was given and later he was shifted to Yenepoya Medical College Hospital, Mangaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as cleaner cum loader in the lorry and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. and Rs.300/- per day as bata.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent no.2 is the insurance policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle
hence, they are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices the respondent No.1 & 2 remained absent and placed exparte.
The Respondent No.3 appeared through its counsel and filed objection statement by denying the issuance of policy to the lorry bearing Reg.No. KA-01-AK-0904.

Further contended that 2nd respondent has issued a cheque bearing No.381193 dated 23.09.2019 for a sum of Rs.1,27,276/-
drawn on Corporation Bank, Neermarga Branch, Mangalore and when the respondent presented the cheque to ICICI Bank, Mangalore the said cheque was dishonoured as funds insufficient with a return memo dated 25.09.2019 hence, this respondent has written a letter to 2 nd respondent informing about the dishonour of cheque and further and informed and declared that the policy issued in favour of 2nd respondent stands cancelled ab initio due to non- receipt of consideration amount hence, this respondent is not liable for any risk.

Further contended that the accident was Harshith Gowda Alias Harshith Kumar K vs Margarate Pereira on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12586575/
2 occurred due to negligence on the part of petitioner himself.

sentences.text: And also denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further this respondent also filed additional written statement admitting issuance of insurance policy to the lorry bearing no. KA-01-AK-0904 and the driver of the said lorry was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and also contended that this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and interest as the 2nd respondent has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
On these grounds, respondent No.3 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of lorry bearing No. KA-01-AK- 0904 by its driver, in RTA took place on 19.03.2020 at about 1.00 a.m. near Vaderahalli gate,
Vaderahalli village, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1, through him got marked Ex.P1 to 10.
Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked documents at Ex.P11 to 16.
Inspite of given sufficient opportunity the respondents failed to adduce evidence.
Hence the respondents evidence is taken as nil.
6. I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;

sentences.text: The Ex.P1 FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Vijay Michael Fernandes.

In the Ex.P2 it is alleged that the driver of the lorry bearing No. KA-01-AK-0904 by driving the said lorry rash and negligently has dashed the another lorry which was proceeding in front of the said offending lorry.
On the basis of Ex.P1- FIR the investigation is conducted by the investigating officer and drawn spot mahazar and rough sketch.
On perusal of rough sketch available in Ex.P3 mahazar the accident place is the left side of the national highway.
The Ex.P5 is the IMV report, wherein it depicts that the front portion of the said offending vehicle has got damaged.
Thus, it evidentiated that the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-0904 has dashed the said lorry by driving the same in rash and negligent manner.

The Ex.P6 charge sheet is also filed against the driver of the lorry bearing No. KA-01-AK-0904.
10.
Admittedly, there is a damage in the front portion of the lorry bearing No. KA-01-AK-0904.
As noted in the spot mahazar and the damages mentioned in Ex.P5 IMV report it is not in dispute.
The petitioner was proceeding as a cleaner in the said lorry.
The Ex.P2 complaint, the petitioner is shown as a cleaner.
No other documents are produced by denying the allegations of the petitioner.

As per the contents of Ex.P.6 charge sheet, the IO has opined that the accident is occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No. KA-01-AK-0904.
11.
As per well settled principle of law the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner sustained injuries in the accident took place on 19.03.2020 which is caused by the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AK-0904 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
12.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :-

The petitioner examined the Medical Record Officer at Adichunchanagiri Hospital as PW.2, through him got marked authorisation letter,
copy of MLC register extract, police intimation and case sheet at Ex.P11 to 14.
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 22 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P8 also shows that the petitioner was aged about 21 years at the time of accident.
In the petition the petitioner has stated that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Yenepoya Medical College Hospital on 19.03.2020 and discharged on 30.03.2020.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7 the petitioner sustained shaft of femur fracture left tibia.
He underwent IMIL nailing femur left side under spinal on 20.3.2020.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Harshith Gowda Alias Harshith Kumar K vs Margarate Pereira on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12586575/

b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P9, amounting to Rs.15,501/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.16,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as cleaner cun loader in the lorry and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. and Rs.300/- per day as bata.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2020.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7- the petitioner was admitted to hospital for a period of 12 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total two months period including 12 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500 X 2 months = Rs.29,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability:- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him, the petitioner has examined Dr.
Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon at Sri Sai Ortho and Dental Centre as PW.3, through him X-ray and clinical report are marked at Ex.P15 & 16.

entities.text: Sri Sai Ortho and Dental Centre
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained fracture of left side femur and he was treated with CRIF with IMIL nail.
He assessed the disability of 47% of to the left lower limb and 16% to the whole body.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
According to the petitioner he was working as cleaner cum loader in the lorry.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 10% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card marked at Ex.P8, as per this document the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 27.2.1999.
The accident was occurred in the year-2020.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 21 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,500/- X 12 X 18 X 10% =Rs.3,13,200/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ; As per Ex.P6 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 12 days.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are simple and grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.

Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for Harshith Gowda Alias Harshith Kumar K vs Margarate Pereira on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12586575/
5 compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards food and nourishment and conveyance.

sentences.text: f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 12 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.
But by considering the nature of the fracture injury sustained by the petitioner as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.12,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: No evidence is placed by the petitioner regarding the need of future medical assistance and expenses.
Hence, he is not entitle for compensation under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 20,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 16,000/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 29,000/-
d) Towards disability Rs. 3,13,200/-
e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 15,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 12,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
h) Towards future medical  expenses NIL  _______________

Liability:-Admittedly the respondent No.2 Harshith Gowda Alias Harshith Kumar K vs Margarate Pereira on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12586575/
6 and 3 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Respondent no.1 is the RC owner.

Initially the written statement is filed by respondent No.3 stating that the cheque issued by the owner for the insurance was dishonoured hence, the policy was cancelled and the same was intimated to the owner and RTO.
But the respondent has not lead any evidence in this regard.
In the charge sheet also no offences are invoked against the owner for not having insurance policy.
The respondent in further additional written statement admitted the issuance of policy.

Hence, the respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.3 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 & 2 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
14.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,25,200/- ( Rupees Four lakhs twenty five thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
